reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the three refunds from the batch appear in the refunds table with matching amounts. I'll check the table first.
All three batch refunds (201, 203, 204) appear in the refunds table with matching amounts, so I can proceed. Next I need the orders to find which customers are owed payouts.
All three batch refunds match the refunds table. The orders show three customers, acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each one's net balance before recording payouts.
Acme's net balance of 54385 matches its orders (39447 + 33625) minus refund 203 (18687). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 29147 matches its orders (4135 + 39885 = 44020) minus refunds 201 (3873) and 204 (11000). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
All three net balances match the orders minus the verified refunds: acme 54385, birch 29147, cobalt 33079 (no refunds). I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout of 54385 was recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 29147 matches its orders minus refunds 201 and 204, which are both in the refunds table. I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 33079 matches its orders 202 (30107) and 205 (2972) with no refunds. Acme and birch are already paid, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches orders minus the verified refunds. Acme 54385, birch 29147, cobalt 33079. The batch is complete.
